title: Sass Small Examples
description: Use these small Sass examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Set up the Sass tool
examples.description: Sass is a tool that turns a style recipe into CSS.
examples.output: The first command adds Sass to a local project. The second prints its version number.

examples.title: Name a colour
examples.description: A Sass variable gives a value a name. The dollar sign starts that name.
examples.output: Both h1 and a rules use #174a8b in the CSS output. The $ink name is replaced during the build.

examples.title: Nest a simple rule
examples.description: Nesting puts a rule inside another rule.
examples.output: The output styles .card and .card h2. Only headings inside a card get the navy colour.

examples.title: Use the parent sign
examples.description: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it.
examples.output: Sass creates .button:focus-visible. A keyboard user can see a clear outline when the button receives focus.

examples.title: Make a mixin recipe
examples.description: A mixin is a named group of CSS choices.
examples.output: Both classes get padding and round corners. Changing the recipe changes both after the next build.

examples.title: Give a mixin an input
examples.description: A mixin can take an input value. A default value is used when the caller does not provide one.
examples.output: The book border is navy. The game border is green because its call supplies a different input.

examples.title: Share a module
examples.description: A module is a Sass file that shares values or recipes.
examples.output: Save the two labelled sections as separate files. Building lesson.scss makes a navy h1 rule.

examples.title: Do simple Sass maths
examples.description: The Sass math module has tools for calculations.
examples.output: The card gets 12px of padding. Sass does the division before the browser loads the page.

examples.title: Use a colour map
examples.description: A map pairs names with values, like labels on paint pots.
examples.output: The note background is gold. The key sun selects that entry from the map.

examples.title: Repeat a small rule
examples.description: An @each loop makes one rule for each item in a list.
examples.output: The output has space-1 with 4px, space-2 with 8px and space-3 with 12px margins.

examples.title: Write a small function
examples.description: A Sass function calculates one value and returns it.
examples.output: The card padding becomes 12px. The return value fits where an ordinary CSS value would go.

examples.title: Build a responsive card
examples.description: Sass can group a screen-size rule with the component it styles.
examples.output: The card has 1rem padding on narrow screens and 2rem when the viewport is at least 40rem wide.
